title: method manifest
description: A method manifest is a flat JSON file of policy differences from today's systematic-review pipeline, plus the claims that policy licenses (docs/ROADMAP.md). It never lists pipeline stages or gates -- those stay in the nine .claude/commands/litreview-*.md files, which are the implementation. tools/method.py globs methods/*.json (except this file and _routing.json) and validates each against this schema.

id.description: Stable identifier, matches the manifest's own filename without the .json extension (e.g. "systematic_review" for methods/systematic_review.json). tools/method.py checks this at load time -- it is not re-derived from the filename.

label.description: Human-readable name shown in reports and CLI output, e.g. "Systematic review".

aliases.description: Other words a reviewer might type for this method (e.g. "SR", "SLR") -- understood by the router (docs/PLAN.md M2), not by this schema.

version.description: Semver, watched by tools/check_framework_version.py -- bump this whenever the manifest's own content changes non-trivially.

family.description: Broad shape of the method, used for routing and for which stage names apply -- not the same as synthesis.families_allowed, which is about pooling. "scoping" (docs/PLAN.md M3) is distinct from "mapping": a scoping review charts studies against a co-developed pack form (capture.mode: charting), while a systematic mapping study classifies them against a frozen facet scheme (capture.mode: classification) -- verified no deterministic tool reads this field yet, so adding a value here is additive and safe.

question_frameworks.description: Research-question frameworks review-protocol may elicit for this method (e.g. PICO, PICo, SPIDER, PCC, or a non-framework label like "Petersen RQs"/"Wieringa research types" for a systematic mapping study).

controlled_vocab.description: Whether this field has an established controlled vocabulary (MeSH-like) to search against. "none" (typical for CS/SE mapping studies) is meant to trigger a QGS (quasi-gold-standard) sensitivity check at S3 (references/docs/design/multi-method-consensus.md §3.2) -- schema only for now, same as synthesis_plan.schema.json's pooling_unit in Phase 0: no tool computes this check yet, so a manifest may declare it without anything enforcing it until a follow-up PR wires search_preflight.py to read it.

schema.description: Repo-relative path to the JSON Schema this method's capture rows must validate against.

ref.description: Repo-relative path to a Markdown reference file under a skill's references/ directory.

when.description: Optional condition (e.g. {"synthesis_family": "swim"}) narrowing when this standard applies.

label_rules.description: The full conduct-floor evaluation of `requires[]` (each `check` backed by one function) is tools/label_gate.py's job (docs/PLAN.md M2) -- in M1 these fields are recorded on the manifest but not yet evaluated.
